prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 1.32. Exact Sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥ ३२ ॥ Exact stored meaning: O Krishna, I desire neither victory nor kingdom nor pleasures. O Govinda, what is a kingdom to us? What are enjoyments? What even is life itself? Chapter context: Before combat on Kurukshetra. Depict the described armies, speakers and events precisely. Dhritarashtra is the blind king listening to Sanjaya in the palace; he is NOT physically on the battlefield. Drona is the elderly martial teacher; Duryodhana is the armored Kaurava king in a muted red cloak. When a verse lists names, render a coherent military group or the stated action, never labeled portrait grids. Krishna and Arjuna have not yet begun the philosophical discourse. No active battle unless the verse actually states it. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O Keshava, I see ill omens and I perceive no good (shreya) in killing my own people in battle. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures — they themselves stand here in battle, having renounced their lives and wealth. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 1.32: O Krishna, I desire neither victory nor kingdom nor pleasures. O Govinda, what is a kingdom to us? What are enjoyments? What even is life itself?
